trust_decision.summary: Whether attacker-controlled part header bytes and the parsed Content-Disposition name/filename (including RFC 2231 percent-decoded values) may carry bare CR/LF into the values busboy/Dicer hand to the application; decided in the vendored Dicer HeaderParser line loop and in the multipart part-header handler after parseParams.

landing_point.why: The summary names the multipart Content-Disposition filename and name; this loop is where fieldname and filename get assigned before they are emitted at lib/types/multipart.js:198 and lib/types/multipart.js:246.

fix_sites.entry_point: public Dicer export (index.js:85): part 'header' event emitted at deps/dicer/lib/Dicer.js:44; also reached by the Busboy multipart path
new Busboy({headers: multipart/form-data}) + write(); 'field'/'file' event fieldname argument
new Busboy({headers: multipart/form-data}) + write(); 'file' event filename argument

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: deps/dicer/lib/HeaderParser.js:117 (exposed as the public Dicer export at index.js:85, header object emitted at deps/dicer/lib/Dicer.js:44)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Dicer is a vendored third-party dependency under deps/ with its own LICENSE, and the advisory names only multipart Content-Disposition name/filename, so a solver can argue that the generic header parser and the raw Dicer API are out of scope; urlencoded keys can be argued to be a different content type where percent-decoding to any byte is standard behaviour.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: RFC 2822 folded header lines (leading SP/HT continuation) must keep being joined, and multipart field values and file bodies may legitimately contain CRLF (textarea input); a fix that rejects CR/LF across the whole header buffer or in part data breaks these. The maxHeaderSize truncation case also changes behaviour (pinned test expects a value of '\r').

O6_input_shapes: bare CR inside a quoted name/filename (fast path parseFormDataDisposition)
bare LF inside a quoted name/filename
bare CR/LF in any part header name or value (Dicer HeaderParser line)
truncated header value ending in CR at the maxHeaderSize limit

O7_producer.where: lib/utils/parseParams.js:591-596 and lib/utils/parseParams.js:609-612 (RFC 2231 percent-decoding into the param value)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: urlencoded body keys are percent-decoded (%0D/%0A) by Decoder and emitted as the 'field' fieldname with no line-break check
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different content type from the advisory's multipart Content-Disposition; percent-decoding to arbitrary bytes is standard urlencoded behaviour and values legitimately carry CRLF.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other file in lib/types, same package as the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: same urlencoded fieldname emission for key=value pairs and at end of stream
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Same as above; it falls together with the first urlencoded route.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other file in lib/types; also lib/types/urlencoded.js:176 and lib/types/urlencoded.js:181

O8b_injection_room.sibling: emit part Content-Type parameters (e.g. charset or name* from parseParams) to the app, with the percent-decoded value left unchecked
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The part Content-Type is already parsed with the same parseParams that does the RFC 2231 decoding, and exposing the mime params is a common feature request.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: extend the fast path parseFormDataDisposition to accept filename*= and percent-decode it itself, bypassing the general loop
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fast path was written for performance and only handles the quoted form; adding the extended form there is a natural optimisation.

O9_family: CRLF / header-value injection (CWE-93) via parsed multipart header parameters

O10_build.toolchain: node + npm; tests via node --test with c8 (100% coverage gate), types via tstyche

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject CR/LF in the raw Content-Disposition header string in multipart.js before parseParams, which misses RFC 2231 %0D/%0A decoding and leaves the public Dicer header object open.

out_of_scope_notes: The README example at README.md:104 joins fieldname into a filesystem path; that is path handling in the docs, not this advisory.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell); tiny_repo is based on the source tree: about 15 small JS files under lib/, deps/ and index.js, with parseParams.js the largest at 625 lines.

Whether the advisory's property covers urlencoded field names (O8) is debatable; the maintainers did not change urlencoded.js, and a hidden test that requires it could be judged unfair. For that reason pattern_fit is A, not A+B.
present_in_latest is unknown for all O8 routes because no latest release was provided.
The advisory text itself was not available; trust decision derived from the summary line and fix diff.
Recall risk is set to low because the advisory was published 2026-10-05; how widely it has been written up since was not checked.
